summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -2 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar 0; brl −; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Class III milk +13.4%; weakest: Oats -14.1%. Key releases ahead: US Federal Funds Rate (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Statement (10-28 2:00 PM ET); US FOMC Press Conference (10-28 2:30 PM ET); US Advance GDP q/q (10-29 8:30 AM ET); US Core PCE Price Index m/m (10-29 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.00% (-11 bp in a month), 2-year 4.69% (-16 bp); 2s10s curve +31 bp (+5 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.03% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.96 (+1.0% in a month, +3.7% YTD). USD/BRL 5.413 (+4.3% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.659 (-0.8%); USD/MXN 18.56 (+4.6%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -0.9% in a month (+12.1% YTD); VIX 18.4. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 102.13 $/bbl (+15.1% in a month), Brent 111.00, ULSD 4.738 $/gal (+8.3%), natural gas 3.02 (-14.4%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -3.3% in a month, Shanghai Composite -4.9%, Hang Seng -5.3%, yuan +0.8% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 13 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (39%); S&P GSCI +2.9% in a month; gold -6.8%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
